title: Ramp / Warm-chain hypothesis journal
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
I started this scratchpad to collect reproducible breadcrumbs and short-lived experiments for the Dedicated GPU pool ramp/warm-chain instability we saw 2025-10-20 → 2025-10-24 (rapid scale-ups then rapid scale-downs, high cold-start latency spikes for customers routed to Dedicated). Goal: capture commands run, raw log excerpts, concrete hypotheses, and next steps to converge on a mitigation we can ship quickly.

High-level observed pattern (timeline):
- 2025-10-20 06:12 UTC: Spike in queued requests across multiple tenants hitting dedicated-pool-east-1; autoscaler triggered +8 nodes (per metrics).
- 2025-10-20 06:16 UTC: We saw multiple warm-chain events: nodes reported READY but serving cold cache for first N requests → long latency (1.2s -> 6s token latency) and some prefetched KV-cache misses.
- 2025-10-20 06:21 UTC: Autoscaler detected low utilization and scaled down -7 nodes within cooldown window (30s), causing another set of requests to fall back to cold nodes. Cycle repeated ~6 times between 06:12–06:30.
- 2025-10-21 to 10-24: recurring similar incidents during bursty load tests + customer traffic.

Commands I ran (quick copy-paste):
- kubectl -n infra logs hpa-controller-7f9b6 --since=1h | grep "scale" | tail -n 200
- kubectl -n serving get deploy dedicated-pool-autoscaler -o yaml > /tmp/dedicated-autoscaler.yaml
- curl -s http://metrics.internal/pools/dedicated-east-1 | jq . | less
- kubectl -n serving exec -it probe-debugger -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -sS http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep warm_chain'

Selected log excerpts (redacted):
- [2025-10-20T06:12:15Z] autoscaler: scale_up target=+8 reason="queued>threshold"
- [2025-10-20T06:13:03Z] node/ded-node-az1-53 ready; warm_chain_start=2025-10-20T06:12:50Z warm_chain_end=2025-10-20T06:13:02Z duration_ms=720
- [2025-10-20T06:14:00Z] router: fallback_to_cold variant=small-gpt2 latency_ms=4800 err=null
- [2025-10-20T06:15:01Z] autoscaler: scale_down target=-7 reason="low_util" cooldown_remaining=25s
- [2025-10-20T06:15:07Z] node/ded-node-az1-47 drain_complete=true active_sessions=0 but cache_populated=false

Raw metric snippets (prometheus-style):
- dedicated_pool_nodes_available{pool="east-1"} 12
- dedicated_pool_nodes_warming{pool="east-1"} 6
- serving_request_queue_length{pool="east-1"} 142
- node_warm_duration_seconds{node="ded-node-az1-53"} 0.72

Error / weirdness notes:
- Several nodes became "Ready" in Kubernetes but logs indicate model KV-cache still being populated asynchronously. Our readiness probe only checks container health and not model cache priming. This means traffic is routed before model is fully primed.
- Autoscaler uses "available_gpus" (node count) and an estimated utilization. It treats a node as available once kubelet marks Ready. There is no notion of "model-serving-warm" in the scaler decision.
- Scale-downs are aggressively triggered when avg_cpu < 10% for 15s. For short bursty traffic that's not enough to capture the transient workload.
- Spot preemptions (we use spot instances in some zones) coincide with a few of the shrink events — but not all.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Readiness vs warm: readiness probes mark nodes Ready before model KV cache completes priming; autoscaler treats Ready as usable -> traffic routed to effectively cold node. This creates apparent "ready but cold" nodes, causing long-tail latencies and immediate utilization drop which triggers scale-downs.
2) Cooldown too short + no warm-state annotation: cooldown window (30s) is shorter than the time it takes for cached-heavy models to show steady utilization. Autoscaler scales down while warm-chain is still priming.
3) Late-binding routing exacerbates things: router sends some requests to newly Ready nodes before they receive any cache-prefill; variance in routing means some tenants see repeated cold hits.
4) Warm-chain latching: when a node enters warm state it blocks eviction for a short time, but our latching is not hooked to actual cache-population metrics; we only latch on "model process started", not on cache_populated=true event.
5) Side effect: preemption + fast scale-downs cause oscillation across AZs as autoscaler tries to re-create capacity in different zones, increasing warm churn.

Quick experiments tried (results):
A) Increased readiness check to include /internal/cache_status (returns {"populated":true/false}).
   - Command: kubectl -n serving patch deploy dedicated-pool --patch "{\"spec\":{\"template\":{\"spec\":{\"containers\": [{\"name\":\"model-server\",\"readinessProbe\":{\"httpGet\":{\"path\":\"/internal/cache_status\",\"port\":9091},\"initialDelaySeconds\":5,\"periodSeconds\":5}}]}}}}"
   - Result: fewer requests routed to cold nodes in a small dev pool; but rollout rolled slowly (helm) and some older nodes still marked Ready because of missing endpoint on older image.
B) Increase scale-down cooldown from 30s -> 120s on autoscaler.
   - Result: reduced oscillation in test cluster. But cost increased and under sustained low load we may keep idle nodes longer than desired.
C) Add jitter to scale decisions (randomized 5-15s) to reduce simultaneous scale-down across AZs.
   - Result: seems to smooth some multi-az flapping during tests.

Data we still need / missing traces:
- Node-level timeline linking: kubelet Ready time vs model server cache_populated event vs router first-request-to-node timestamp. We need a single view that correlates those three for a representative incident.
- Full autoscaler decision trace (input metrics at time t, internal threshold evals). Need HPA logs + controller internal metrics.
- Which images/nodes used spot vs on-demand during the incident.

Short-term mitigations to try (low-risk):
- Safety: patch readiness probe to require cache_populated=true before marking container Ready in Dedicated pools (roll as feature flag).
- Autoscaler: extend scale-down cooldown to 90-120s for dedicated pools with cache-heavy models. Add a min-ready-standing-time annotation before scale-down.
- Router: sticky routing to avoid bouncing same tenant to brand-new nodes within first N requests (N=10).
- Deploy a lightweight metric: node_model_warm{node="..."} -> expose to autoscaler and router; on warm=false treat node as unavailable for new requests.

Longer-term design ideas (bigger work):
- Make autoscaler "warm aware": add a warm_state metric and prefer scaling based on effective-serving-capacity (nodes * warm_factor).
- Prewarm pool: keep small pool of prewarmed nodes (min_warm=2 per AZ) for hot models.
- Improve placement policy to consider model-weighted startup cost (large transformers get scheduled on capacity where we maintain a warm cache).

Concrete next steps / owners / timeline:
- [ASAP] Patch readiness probe to require cache_populated flag in Dedicated pools (Maya) — target canary on dev-dedicated-pool by 2025-10-29.
- [48h] Increase scale-down cooldown to 90s for dedicated pools (Noah) — monitor cost/oscillation tradeoff.
- [72h] Add minimal router stickiness for first-10-requests (Ethan) — quick config flip in router for dedicated routing policy.
- [1 week] Instrumentation: build single trace view correlating kubelet Ready / cache_populated / first-request (Maya + Noah).

Open questions / risks:
- How many different models is this affecting? Heavy models only (large-context decoders) or all? We need model-level sampling.
- If readiness depends on model cache endpoint, what happens on older images that don't expose it? Need migration strategy.
- Cost vs reliability: longer cooldown reduces oscillation but raises baseline cost. Estimate cost delta before changing globally.

Notes to self: keep this focused on Dedicated pools (don't apply same tuning to Hosted multitenant without more thought). Save copies of the above log snippets to /tmp/incident-20251020 for quick replay.

If you see this and have extra logs or traces (router traces, kube events, spot termination history), paste them below.

-- end of scratchpad --
